How much should I budget for carpet installation in North Bend, WA?

Plan on $4 to $7 per square foot installed — carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away included. Most North Bend projects come in between $2,000 and $4,500, and a 1,200 sq ft main floor with a staircase usually lands between $5,500 and $8,500. The grade of carpet you pick moves the price more than anything else, and you pick it from samples laid out in your own rooms.
Does the mobile carpet showroom really come out to North Bend?

Yes — the van covers the whole upper valley. It shows up with 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades, and we lay them on the exact floors they would cover, so you judge color in your own light rather than a store's. Every room and stair gets measured the same visit, you keep a written price, and the trip costs you nothing.
What does carpet stretching cost in North Bend?

Carpet stretching starts at $99 per room in North Bend. A power stretcher pulls ripples, waves and bunched spots back out flat, and it runs about a fifth of what replacement costs — so when the pile still stands up and you still like the color, stretching is the smart money.
How much do carpeted stairs cost in North Bend?

Stair carpet starts at $18 per step, installed waterfall style or wrapped cap-and-band. Landings and pie-shaped winders — common in the valley's two-story floor plans — are measured and written into the quote at the visit rather than billed as an extra afterward.
How long does the install actually take?

One day handles most North Bend homes. Three or four rooms plus a staircase is a comfortable single day for the crew; a whole house with stairs and heavy furniture can spill into a second. Either way, the schedule goes on your written quote so you can plan around it.
Will the installers move my furniture?

Yes. Beds, dressers, couches and tables are included on most jobs, and everything goes back where it stood once the carpet is in. We ask you to clear the small things ahead of time — closet floors, electronics, breakables, and anything you'd rather carry yourself.
Stretch my carpet, or replace it?

Stretch it when the pile stands up, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room — that's a $99-per-room fix instead of a full re-carpet. Replace it when traffic lanes are matted flat, seams are letting go, the backing is breaking down, or pet odor has survived a professional cleaning. We look first and tell you which side yours is on.
Which North Bend neighborhoods do you cover?

All of them — downtown North Bend, Si View, Forster Woods, Tanner, Riverbend, Cedar Falls, Wilderness Rim, Edgewick, Maloney Grove and Sallal Prairie — plus Snoqualmie, Snoqualmie Ridge, Fall City, Preston and up toward Snoqualmie Pass. Farther out, say along the Middle Fork road? Ask when you book; the van usually still comes.
What carpet is best for muddy dogs?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, laid over a moisture-barrier pad. The color runs all the way through the fiber, so it takes hard cleaning — even diluted bleach — without fading, and the barrier pad keeps accidents out of the subfloor, which is where permanent odor starts. After a muddy season of Mount Si hikes, that combination earns its keep. Upgrading to that pad starts at $0.65 per square foot.
What's the warranty on the installation work?

OC Flooring backs every installation with a 1-year workmanship warranty, and the carpet carries its mill warranty on top — usually 10 to 25 years on wear and stain, depending on grade. Both go on your written quote. Worth knowing: mills can tie their coverage to the pad underneath, which is one more reason all three pad grades come along to the visit.
